- Right portion: kernels completely blackened/shrunken with dark material
- Left portion: tan/yellow kernels with some dark spots scattered
- Some white material mixed among kernels
- No fleshy white galls visible — kernels appear to be directly turning black

Top candidates: **Common_smut**, **Head_smut**, **Ear_rots_General_Mixed**

Let me view reference images for the top candidates.

The Common_smut reference shows fleshy green galls — doesn't match. Head_smut shows dry spore masses with vascular strands. Ear_rots_General_Mixed reference shows ears with mixed tan-to-black kernel patterns — very similar to test image!

Let me check a few more candidates to confirm.

Analysis of reference images:
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Shows dark husk damage, not individual kernel blackening — doesn't match
- **Fusarium**: White cottony mold on yellow/tan kernels — doesn't match the extensive blackening
- **Ear_rots_Trichoderma**: Green/blue-green mold between kernels — doesn't match
- **Ear_rots_General_Mixed**: Shows ears with kernels transitioning from tan/normal to completely black — **strong visual match** to test image

The test image shows:
- Corn ear with husks pulled back
- Kernels on one end completely black and shrunken
- Remaining kernels tan/yellow with some dark spots scattered
- Mixed rot pattern with multiple discoloration patterns
- No single-type mold (not pink, not green, not white cottony)

This matches **Ear_rots_General_Mixed** — the reference images show exactly this pattern of mixed kernel discoloration from tan to completely black across the ear.
